raw:
I checked all 19 races of the 2014 season, using each race's top-10 results with starting grid positions. The pole sitter (grid 1) won 9 of them:

| Race | Winner | Grid |
|---|---|---|
| Malaysia | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| China | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| Spain | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| Monaco | Rosberg | 1 ✔ |
| Germany | Rosberg | 1 ✔ |
| Italy | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| Singapore | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| Russia | Hamilton | 1 ✔ |
| Brazil | Rosberg | 1 ✔ |

The other 10 races were won by a driver who did not start from pole: Australia (Rosberg, grid 3), Bahrain (Hamilton, grid 2), Canada (Ricciardo, grid 6), Austria (Rosberg, grid 3), Britain (Hamilton, grid 6), Hungary (Ricciardo, grid 4), Belgium (Ricciardo, grid 5), Japan (Hamilton, grid 2), USA (Hamilton, grid 2) and Abu Dhabi (Hamilton, grid 2).

As a cross-check, the race-by-race winners add up to the final standings (Hamilton 11 wins, Rosberg 5, Ricciardo 3).

ANSWER: 9
